findings.description: The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects (including the uploaded vendor roster) are stored without an enforced encryption policy or customer-managed key.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or explicit private ACL is configured for this bucket, leaving it reliant on account defaults and vulnerable to accidental public ACL or policy grants.
Server access logging is not enabled, so unauthorised access to the archived reports and the seeded vendor roster would leave no audit trail.
Versioning is not enabled, so objects can be silently overwritten or deleted (combined with force_destroy = true) with no recoverable prior state, weakening tamper resistance.
This bucket holds ledger exports (financial data) but defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so data at rest is not protected by an enforced KMS or SSE policy.
The bucket relies only on a private ACL with no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so a future bucket policy or ACL change could expose financial ledger data publicly.
No logging block is configured for a bucket containing sensitive ledger exports, eliminating forensic visibility into data access.
Versioning is disabled while force_destroy is true, so ledger export objects can be permanently deleted or overwritten without recovery.
The model artifacts bucket has versioning and logging but no server-side encryption configuration, leaving stored artifacts unencrypted by default.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource restricts public ACLs or policies on this bucket, so accidental public exposure of model artifacts is possible.
Operational runbooks, which frequently contain internal procedures and sensitive operational detail, are stored without any server-side encryption configuration.
The bucket sets a private ACL but has no public access block, leaving no defence-in-depth control against future public policy or ACL grants.
No server access logging is configured, so reads of the runbooks bucket are not recorded for audit purposes.
The audit log destination bucket uses the log-delivery-write ACL but has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so audit evidence could be exposed by a future ACL or policy misconfiguration.
force_destroy = true on the audit log bucket allows all audit evidence to be deleted along with the bucket, undermining log integrity and non-repudiation.

A vendor roster spreadsheet (likely containing third-party PII/commercial data) is uploaded from the repository into a bucket with no default encryption, and the object itself specifies no kms_key_id or server_side_encryption.
No bucket policy denying non-TLS (aws:SecureTransport = false) requests is attached to this or any other bucket in the file, permitting cleartext HTTP access to stored data.
